title: Entropy-based sampling for usage exports to control customer costs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Large customers with high request volumes incur significant egress and storage costs for scheduled CSV/S3 usage exports and webhook deliveries. We need a configurable, auditable sampling layer that reduces export size while preserving representativity for billing, anomaly detection, and customer-facing reports.

Goal: Implement an entropy-aware sampling engine in the export pipeline that produces deterministic, per-tenant sampled exports. Sampling must be:
- deterministic across retries and resumptions (seeded by tenant_id + calendar-window)
- configurable per-subscription (sample_rate, stratification keys like model_id/route, min-retention thresholds)
- explainable (export manifest contains sampling metadata + correction factors)
- compatible with CSV, Parquet, and webhook deliveries

Proposed approach:
1) Add a SamplingStage to the export pipeline that runs after canonicalization and redaction but before row serialization. The stage computes a hash-based pseudo-random value per row using a tenant-scoped seed. Rows are kept if hash % denominator < numerator where denominator is derived from sample_rate.
2) Support stratified sampling by allowing export subscription to declare 1..N stratification keys (default: model_id). The SamplingStage maintains proportional quotas per stratum for each window to avoid losing low-frequency but important strata.
3) Emit a sampling_report JSON blob alongside each export (and include pointers to it in the manifest) containing: sample_rate, seed, strata counts (pre/post), and an approximate correction multiplier per stratum for downstream analysts to recompute estimates.
4) UI/Config: extend export subscription schema to accept sampling config; default is off for existing subscriptions. Provide migration tooling to preview sampled export sizes before enabling.
5) Observability: emit metrics (sampled_rows, pre_sample_rows, strata_underflow_alert) and a dashboard for customers and internal ops to validate representativity.
6) Backfill/Replay: when a full export is required (for audits or billing disputes), allow a "no-sampling" replay mode within the retention window; record audit events when replay is requested.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Deterministic hash sampling is efficient and resumable, but may bias if tenant traffic has non-random ordering; stratification mitigates this.
- More sophisticated sampling (e.g., reservoir sampling with priority weights) provides higher-quality representativity for heavy-tailed data but is stateful and complicates resumability and horizontal scaling. We propose hash+strata as a pragmatic first step.
- Sampling affects downstream customers who perform exact accounting. We will provide correction factors and clear UI disclaimers; for billing/legal needs, full exports remain available on request.

Acceptance criteria:
- SamplingStage implemented and feature-flagged in export pipeline.
- Export manifest contains sampling metadata and links to sampling_report.
- Per-subscription sampling config is persisted and validated in the API.
- Dashboard and metrics exist to monitor pre/post sampling distributions and detect strata underflow.
- E2E test that verifies determinism across retry/resume and stratification correctness for synthetic data.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/entropy-sampling-design
- Spike notebook (Drive): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/usage-export-sampling-spike
- Proto/Schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4527
- Draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/exports/sampling-preview

Rollout plan: start with internal exports (redwood-internal tenants) behind a feature flag for 2 weeks; then beta with opt-in customer subscriptions; finally GA with opt-out controls and a clear communications plan for customers that rely on full exports.
comments: 2026-03-11: Spike completed. Notebook demonstrates hash-seed approach yields stable 5% sample across 30-day window for synthetic tenant. Link above.
2026-03-12: Design review with PM and Privacy attended. Agreed to keep default sampling off and require explicit opt-in. PM asked for a preview size estimation API before enabling on a subscription.
2026-03-13: Marcus implemented a prototype SamplingStage; initial perf numbers show <4% additional CPU for export runner under 100k rows/window. Need to validate under heavy multi-tenant concurrency.
2026-03-14: Security asked for audit log entry when replay/no-sampling mode is used. Added to acceptance criteria and queued a small follow-up task (ENG-21878) for audit implementation.
